auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Throughout this work, we assume that any treatment-specific variable can only be affected by past treatments or past covariates; and not the future. This is sometimes called temporal ordering. We also assume a “no interference” setting and Assumption 1 below (Murphy, 2003; Robins, 1987, 2000a).

auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
The DTE between any treatment paths $\bar a_T,\bar a'_T\in\{0,1\}^T$ is now defined as
\[
\theta:=E[Y(\bar a_T)]-E[Y(\bar a'_T)]=\theta_{\bar a_T}-\theta_{\bar a'_T}.
\]
auxiliary_passages.resolution: The stage-zero conditional mean theta_a-bar-T is the expected potential outcome. This resolves the terminal/initial conventions of D33 without importing the two-stage treatment model.

auxiliary_passages.statement_original: The above result is of independent interests as it provides a general theory for any Lasso estimators based on imputed outcomes. It contributes to the literature in three specific aspects: (a) The “imputation error”, $\widehat Y_i-Y_i^*$, can be dependent on and even possibly correlated with covariates $\mathbf X_i$; (b) We allow every $\widehat Y_i$ to be fitted using the same set of observations $(\mathbf X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^M$, i.e., $\widehat Y_i$s are also possibly dependent on each other; and (c) The tuning parameter $\lambda_M$ is of the same order as the one chosen for the fully observed data and is independent of the imputation error or any sparsity parameter.
auxiliary_passages.resolution: Confirms that independence is imposed on the original observations, not on the imputed responses or their errors. The source uses Y_i, not Y_i-star, in the descriptive training-set tuple; this is retained.

unresolved_source_conventions.detail: The inspected source is arXiv:2110.04924v4, 16 May 2023. Its title and authors identify the corpus paper, but equality with the 2024 journal typesetting is not established.

The main paper ends before the embedded supplement on page 26. No appendix results or definitions are used. A boundary crop from earlier intake exposed introductory supplementary prose; it is not retained or used as extraction evidence. The final boundary image contains only the supplement title.

unresolved_source_conventions.detail: The rate prints s2, but the subsequent definition names s2-prime. That definition also uses the indicator mu_a,NR-star != mu_a despite the S-DRL setting. Both are retained; there is a literal local dependency on the nested target and no silent s2 or model-symbol repair.

The argument eta binds delta without a path subscript, but the final denominator prints delta_c. A path-specific interpretation is plausible, but no substitution is made in the original score formula.

Both theorems print {E[mu-hat-mu-star]^r}^{1/r} without absolute-value bars, for any constant r>=1. For noninteger r and signed errors this lacks an ordinary real-valued interpretation. Neither expression is rewritten as an absolute moment or Lr norm.

Theorem 10 cites Assumptions 1-3 without the explicit replacement of mu-star and beta-star by their NR counterparts used in Theorems 4-5. Its literal reference to Assumption 2 is preserved. Whether a nested-model substitution was intended remains unresolved; the resulting DR-target dependence is not concealed.

The reference to r_n in Theorem 9(c) resolves only the expression used in the bound. Theorem 10 does not explicitly assume nu-star=nu, Assumption 4 or the DR inner-split fitting method; these are not imported through the reference.

The procedures loop over both a and a-prime, and residuals/score contrasts include both paths. Many displayed regularity and sparsity conditions are written only with subscript a, without an explicit max over the two paths. The audit preserves that wording; it does not add an unstated uniform quantifier or maximum to the original theorem.

Theorem 2 through Theorem 5 do not print explicit tuning-rate choices for the four penalties. Their algorithms refer to objectives with positive penalties; Theorems 9-10 separately state tuning rates for the nuisance fits. The latter rates are not retroactively inserted into earlier theorem statements.

Equal K-fold sizes and, in Algorithm 1, equal inner halves require divisibility. Section 2.4 explicitly treats n=N/K as an integer; Algorithm 1 does not supply a rounding convention. K>=2 is printed but no growth regime for K is specified in the inventoried limit statements.

The score scale can shrink to zero asymptotically. Exact positivity of sigma is not explicitly asserted in Assumption 2, although reciprocal normalizations and rates divided by sigma require it; Assumption 5 also has ratios with residual second moments in denominators. No zero-denominator convention is supplied or invented.

The source defines the squared score contrast centered at the true theta. Under arbitrary misspecification this need not be the variance centered at its own expectation. The squared-moment definition is retained even where the source uses variance terminology.

The terminal working mean is defined as mu-star_(T+1)(s-bar_(T+1),a-bar_T):=s_(T+1). No separate scalar coordinate s_(T+1) is defined beforehand, while the next sentence explicitly identifies the terminal working and true means with Y under consistency. Both sentences are retained; the last-outcome-coordinate interpretation is recorded, not substituted into the original.

The overlap probability contains lower-case s-bar_t rather than random S-bar_t. This differs from Assumption 1(c), which uses random covariates. The source argument is preserved without changing the scope to a pointwise or almost-sure condition.

Theorem 11 states t<=T-1 without a lower bound. The following discussion explicitly includes t=0; the stage-zero empty-history convention supports that case. Negative times are not defined and are not added as meaningful inputs.

The source writes argmin objects without a universal tie-breaking or existence convention for every input. Conditional expectations evaluated at specified covariates require versions, with no all-point version selection specified. These are recorded formalization prerequisites, not repaired definitions.

The theorem defines epsilon_i and then bounds the unindexed epsilon Orlicz norm. The natural independent-copy residual Y-star-X-transpose beta-star is supported by the pre-theorem independent-copy setup, but is not explicitly defined in the theorem body.

The gauge formula is stated for x>0, whereas the norm evaluates it at |X|/c, possibly zero. Extending exp(x^alpha)-1 to zero is conventional, but the printed domain restriction is not silently rewritten.
